label: CONTRASTIVE_BAYESIAN_COMPARISON_1: Two mutually exclusive and exhaustive hypotheses W and V…
definition: Two mutually exclusive and exhaustive hypotheses W and V, rational prior p with 0<p<1, and positive likelihoods at most one for the same received event. The normalizer is p*lW+(1-p)*lV; posteriorW and posteriorV divide these weighted likelihoods by the normalizer. The likelihood ratio lW/lV greater than one supports W in the strict posterior-probability-increase sense; a ratio less than one is evidence against W and reduces its probability, while a ratio equal to one is neutral and preserves the prior. Posterior preference between W and V also depends on the prior. Community is an ignored argument of publicAssessment; swap complements prior and exchanges likelihoods.
